transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-03
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (EchoHealth - Procurement), Tom Baker (EchoHealth - Legal), Priya Singh (EchoHealth - CTO), Sam Ortiz (EchoHealth - Eng Manager)

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh, really appreciate you making time. I'm Lena from Redwood. With me is Marco, our SE. Quick round-robin?
[00:07] Aisha: Hi, Aisha here. I lead procurement. We'll probably take notes on the legal and security bits.
[00:10] Tom: Tom Baker, legal counsel. I'll be focused on data residency and the DPA specifics.
[00:13] Priya: Priya, CTO. I'll chime in on architecture and the pilot.
[00:16] Marco: Marco Ruiz, solutions engineer. I'll handle the SOC2/KMS questions and onboarding.
[00:20] Sam: Sam, engineering manager, will be running the pilot with our infra team.

[00:24] Lena: Great. The agenda we circulated was MSA/DPA redlines, SLA and uptime, security docs, and an onboarding timeline — plus pricing approval. Sound good?
[00:30] Aisha: Yep. Good.

-- Auto summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect) --
[00:35] Speaker 1: discussed MSA terms, DPA obligations, token retention, vendor onboarding and PO sequence, unclear capture of "KV cash" reference, and mention of dedicated vs hosted.

[00:45] Tom: To start, we reviewed the MSA. We have two primary exceptions: liability cap language and a clause on export controls / data residency in EMEA. Also want more clarity on subprocessors in the DPA.
[00:58] Lena: Totally. On the liability cap we usually have standard clauses, but for enterprise we can discuss an increase and carve-outs. About subprocessors, Marco, can you cover how Redwood lists and notifies subprocessors?
[01:08] Marco: Sure — we maintain a subprocessors list in our compliance portal; we notify customers 30 days ahead for major changes, and we have subprocessor agreements in place. For DPA purposes we can add EchoHealth to the subscription for notifications.
[01:22] Tom: 30 days is acceptable. For certain categories we might ask for prior approval, not just notice — particularly for hosting in APAC.
[01:31] Priya: On the hosting side, just to clarify, our initial pilot wants a VPC-private deployment in us-west, with optional on-prem later. We don't want logs leaving region.
[01:40] Marco: Understood. We support Private deployments (VPC or on-prem). For VPC, control plane metadata can be customer-managed; data plane remains in the region you choose. We can include region restrictions in the DPA for the pilot.
[01:54] Sam: How does key management look — we want to use our KMS (HSM) keys, not Redwood-managed keys.
[02:01] Marco: We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS / Cloud HSM). There are a couple small config steps in the onboarding. We'll provide diagrams.

[02:12] Aisha: On SLAs — uptime and credits — what's standard? We need 99.9% target but also clear credits schedule.
[02:20] Lena: Redwood's default SLA for Dedicated/Private is 99.9%. For hosted, we quote typical numbers in the deck. We can put 99.9% in the MSA for the pilot. Credits structure is typically pro-rated service credits for downtime windows above threshold. I can attach the SLA schedule to the redline.
[02:36] Tom: We'll need definitions — what counts as downtime, scheduled maintenance notification windows, and force majeure carve-outs.
[02:44] Marco: Yep, we can add maintenance windows and scheduled maint notices — usually 48 hours for planned maintenance for Private deployments, shorter for hosted.

[02:55] Priya: One thing — can you confirm there is a graceful fallback if Dedicated capacity hits pressure? We can't have spikes break our flow.
[03:03] Marco: Yes — smart routing can failover to a compatible variant or queue depending on your policy, but fallbacks are configurable. For Private, we can discuss reserved capacity or dedicated pools and burst policies in Redwood Dedicated.
[03:16] Priya: Good.

[03:20] Aisha: Pricing approvals — we need to route the contract through finance. Does Redwood accept standard PO terms? We have a 30 net invoice term.
[03:29] Lena: We accept POs; net-30 is standard for self-serve, for enterprise we often do net-45 or net-60 depending on negotiation, but we can accommodate net-30 once pricing is approved. I'll note PO contact details.
[03:41] Aisha: I'll share the procurement approval timeline after this call.

[03:45] Tom: On data processing, one specific ask: DPA should state we retain no customer data beyond cache requirements, and there should be an ability to request data deletion on termination with certificate of deletion.
[03:57] Marco: We do support data deletion and can provide deletion certificates. For KV cache / prompt caching, we have TTL controls; also note that model outputs may be logged for quality unless disabled — we can opt-out for EchoHealth.
[04:10] Tom: Great, opt-out is required for us. Please note that.

[04:15] Lena: We'll mark the DPA to state opt-out of telemetry and logs for EchoHealth.
[04:19] Sam: A quick note from eng: what's the estimated lead time to spin up a private VPC pilot with 2 GPUs and a trial RPS?
[04:26] Marco: For Private VPC in us-west with reserved 2-GPU nodes, once the MSA is signed and we have onboarding info, typical provisioning is 7-10 business days. If you need faster, Dedicated reserved capacity can be pre-provisioned but may require deposit.
[04:41] Priya: Can you provide a checklist of required network configs and firewall rules?
[04:45] Marco: Absolutely — I'll send the onboarding checklist and the architecture diagram listing ports, CIDRs, and KMS endpoints.

[04:52] Lena: Pricing question from earlier — for the pilot do we have a trial credit or pilot rate?
[04:57] Marco: Yes, we typically offer a 30-day pilot credit and a reduced pilot rate for reserved trial capacity; Lena will include the pricing sheet.
[05:06] Aisha: For procurement to sign, we need two things: the redlined MSA/DPA and a clear pricing worksheet that shows month 1 expected spend for the pilot.
[05:15] Lena: We'll provide both.

[05:20] Tom: On subprocessors — you mentioned a portal. Can you confirm subprocessor list includes cloud providers and any third-party monitoring vendors? We want transparency.
[05:29] Marco: Yes — cloud infra providers (e.g., AWS) and monitoring/observability vendors are listed. We'll provide the current snapshot and cadence for updates.
[05:36] Tom: Also want to know retention of logs for a security incident. If we ask for forensics, what's your retention window by default?
[05:44] Marco: Default retention is 90 days for operational logs; we can extend retention longer under a contract addendum. For security incidents we retain relevant traces as per our incident response policy, and we can preserve snapshots on request.

[05:58] Priya: Regarding encryption in transit — TLS 1.2+? And are there mutual TLS options?
[06:03] Marco: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 supported; mutual TLS is available for Private deployments. We'll put details in the security packet.

[06:10] Aisha: Another procurement note: we have an internal requirement to validate SOC2 Type II. Can you provide the report and the scope?
[06:17] Marco: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II — scope includes change management, access controls, and incident response for the service. I'll attach the report and the scope summary.

[06:26] Tom: And pen test reports? We prefer at least annual testing.
[06:29] Marco: We have annual external pen tests and internal code scanning. We'll share the redacted executive summary of the latest test.

[06:37] Sam: Ok, switching to timeline: if MSA signed by 2025-12-10, what's realistic for pilot start?
[06:43] Marco: If signed by 12-10, provisioning 7-10 business days — pilot could start around 12-22 to 12-24 if no holiday delays. Otherwise earliest in Jan after holidays.
[06:52] Priya: Keep in mind our finance cycle closes 12-18, so we ideally want PO by 12-15.
[06:57] Aisha: I'll push for internal approvals to hit that date.

[07:03] Lena: Any legal redlines you want to preview now?
[07:06] Tom: The two we mentioned: liability cap increase request and prior approval for certain subprocessors. Also seeking a deletion certificate clause. Lastly, we need EMEA data residency language for patients in EU.
[07:18] Marco: For region restrictions we can add a DPA clause to bind the data plane to the chosen region and exclude other regions. We'll include export control language.
[07:27] Lena: We'll deliver a redline that addresses the three items and show where we can be flexible.

[07:31] Priya: One more technical — what telemetry do you gather by default? We want to know exactly what's sent to Redwood for model quality monitoring.
[07:38] Marco: Default telemetry includes request/response metadata, latency metrics, and optionally anonymized prompts for quality. For EchoHealth we agreed to opt out of telemetry and we can collect only essential logs for billing and SLOs.
[07:52] Tom: Make sure that opt-out is explicit in the DPA and that we can turn it on/off per environment.
[07:58] Marco: Noted.

[08:01] Lena: Okay — recap before we close: Redwood to send redlined MSA+DPA, SOC2 and pen test summary, onboarding checklist and architecture diagram, and pricing worksheet. EchoHealth to confirm procurement timeline and provide PO contact. Schedule security deep dive for week of 12-08. Is that accurate?
[08:15] Aisha: Yes.
[08:16] Tom: Yes.
[08:17] Priya: Yes.
[08:18] Sam: Yep.

[08:20] Lena: Great — we'll get those artifacts out. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the security deep dive.
[08:26] Aisha: Thanks.
[08:27] Tom: Thank you.
[08:28] Marco: Thanks all.

-- End transcript --

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-transcription of product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated"), "KV cash" vs "KV cache" noted in auto summary. Occasional overlapping talk markers removed for readability.
